topics.title: Exam Core: What Will Be Asked
The I, the A and the G

modes.blurb: Ten questions, like the real paper.
modes.why: The real midterm is ten questions with two ruled lines each. This draws ten across the topics in proportion to their marks. The clock is for pacing practice, not the exam's real duration.

modes.title: Exam core
modes.blurb: Only what is most likely on Friday's paper.
modes.why: A narrow pass over the handful of questions the examiner's blueprint and past papers point at, with model two-line answers.

modes.title: Abbreviations
modes.blurb: MLP, CNN, VAE, GAN, GPT: expand it and say what the letter means.
modes.why: Acronym unpacking is the cheapest mark on the paper, and a misread letter (the G in AGI vs GAI) is the commonest way to lose it.

modes.title: Tell them apart
modes.blurb: AE or VAE? Gradient descent or backprop?
modes.why: Two ruled lines per answer means the marks sit in the clause that separates a term from its neighbour. This is the highest-yield drill in the course.

modes.title: The six architectures
modes.blurb: MLP, CNN, VAE, U-Net, Transformer, Diffusion.
modes.why: The examiner's own blueprint line reads 'Architectures: Multi-Layer Perceptron, Convolutional NN, VAE, ..' — know each one's key idea and where it sits on the predictive-to-generative arc.

modes.title: Names and dates
modes.blurb: Who did what, and roughly when.
modes.why: The course is attribution-heavy on both sides, and a name plus a year is the cheapest half of a two-line answer.
